questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: When multiple wells are pumped close together, well interference leads to:
options: A single well lowers the water level only within its own circle of influence
Multiple wells → cone superposition. Additional drawdown. Reduced yield
Pumping one well raises the water level in all neighbouring wells
Interference appears only when the wells are tapping different aquifers
questions.solution: Interference: s_total = Σs_i. Spacing wells to minimize. Constant rate vs constant drawdown.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Stereographic projection represents crystal faces as which elements plotted on a Wulff net?
options: Gnomonic. A projection that preserves areas but distorts all angular relations between faces
Great circles and poles. Wulff (equal-angle) net. Angle between crystal faces measured
Orthographic. A projection showing the crystal as seen from a distant point along the axis
Equidistant. A projection in which angular distances are measured along straight lines
questions.solution: Stereographic: 2D representation of 3D angles. Measured on goniometer. Rotation about N-S axis.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: We currently live in which geological era?
options: Cenozoic
Mesozoic
Precambrian
Palaeozoic
questions.solution: The Cenozoic ('age of mammals') is the present era, following the Mesozoic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Glossopteris flora: distribution in Gondwana:
options: Permian seed fern found in India, Australia, Antarctica, Africa, South America
Restricted to the Northern Hemisphere, where it dominates the Carboniferous swamp forests
Cosmopolitan, occurring in both hemispheres throughout the whole of the Phanerozoic
Confined to shallow marine shelves, where it grew as a floating algal mat
questions.solution: Glossopteris: Gondwana indicator. Found in coal measures. Key evidence for continental drift.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Cenozoic Era is characterized by which major biological and climatic developments?
options: Mammal diversification and growth of ice sheets
Dominance of reptiles across all terrestrial habitats
Peak radiation of marine invertebrates in shelf seas
Termination of all plate tectonic activity
questions.solution: Cenozoic: Age of Mammals. India-Asia collision (Himalaya), Antarctic glaciation, grassland expansion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ore deposit models: porphyry Cu-Mo vs porphyry Cu-Au:
options: Cu-Au deposits form exclusively in S-type granite terranes with reduced magmas
Both deposit types form in identical settings with identical magma compositions
Cu-Mo deposits derive from reduced ilmenite-series magmas rich in tin
Cu-Mo: I-type, oxidized. Cu-Au: magnetite-rich, reduced
questions.solution: Porphyry Cu-Mo: calc-alkaline, I-type. Cu-Au: more oxidized, magnetite-rich. Kalgoorlie type.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Stable isotope δ18O in marine carbonates reflects:
options: Temperature and water composition
Only atmospheric pressure
Only salinity of surface runoff
Only the concentration of dissolved sulphate
questions.solution: δ18O: temperature proxy. Higher δ18O = colder (or more ice). Also reflects seawater composition changes.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Granulite facies metamorphism occurs under what approximate temperature and pressure, and with which mineral assemblage?
options: T < 300°C, low P. Hydrous minerals such as chlorite and muscovite stable
Very high P (>15 kbar), low T. Stable along subduction zones
T 400-500°C, moderate P. Biotite and amphibole remain stable
T > 700°C, P 3-10 kbar. Anhydrous minerals (pyroxene, garnet, feldspar)
questions.solution: Granulite: dry conditions. H₂O absent. Pyroxene + garnet + feldspar. Lower crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The eclogite facies of metamorphism indicates what range of pressure conditions?
options: Very high pressure conditions
Low pressure and high temperature conditions
Shallow burial in an extensional setting
Contact metamorphism near an igneous intrusion
questions.solution: Eclogite: omphacite + garnet. Very high P (>1.2 GPa), moderate to high T. Indicative of subduction zone depths.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the age, basement relation, and internal subdivision of the Cuddapah Basin?
options: Cenozoic (66 Ma to present) foreland basin filled with thick terrestrial molasse deposits of the shallow shelf
Mesozoic (Triassic-Jurassic) rift basin with coal measures and plant fossils of Glossopteris
Archean basement complex with greenstone belts and tonalite-trondhjemite gneiss of the craton
Proterozoic (1.6-0.6 Ga). Unconformably overlies Dharwar. Papaghni + Chitravati + Nallamalai + Srisailam
questions.solution: Cuddapah: Chevron fold belt (Nallamalai). Pb-Zn at Zawar (Rajasthan). Uranium at Lambapur.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Inselberg is an erosional remnant composed of:
options: Resistant rock (granite/gneiss)
Soft unconsolidated alluvial fan material
Wind-deposited loess and volcanic ash
Marine sediment of a coastal lowland
questions.solution: Inselberg: isolated hill rising from plain. Erosional remnant of resistant rock. Common in arid tropical regions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does seismic hazard assessment typically provide for engineering design?
options: Ground motion prediction. PGA, response spectra. Site effects (liquefaction, amplification)
Seismic hazard considers only the depth of the water table beneath the construction site and its vicinity
Seismic hazard is determined only by the local weathering state of the rocks
Groundwater conditions alone control the seismic hazard of a construction site
questions.solution: Seismic: active faults, historical seismicity. Zonation maps. Microzonation for critical projects.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In vorticity analysis, the rotation of rigid porphyroclasts within a ductile matrix is used to assess:
options: Volume change measured from pressure shadows around rigid grains
Temperature of deformation recorded by metamorphic mineral assemblages and growth zoning in porphyroblasts
Strain only, ignoring the rotation of material lines and rigid objects
Porphyroclast rotation. Rigid grains in ductile matrix. Rotational vs non-rotational deformation
questions.solution: Vorticity number W_k: simple shear (1), pure shear (0), general (0-1). Hyperbolic flow.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Aeolian sand transport: saltation height:
options: About 10–20 meters above the surface
Always exactly one meter above the surface
Always less than one millimeter high
Typically <1 meter above surface
questions.solution: Saltation: bouncing grains. Trajectory height <1m. Creep: surface rolling. Suspension: fine particles.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Assimilation and fractional crystallization (AFC):
options: Mixing of two coeval mantle-derived magmas within a single chamber
Pure fractional crystallization of a single parental magma with no interaction with the wall rocks
Wholesale melting of the country rock with no crystallization taking place
Country rock assimilation + fractional crystallization. Combined effect. DePaolo equations
questions.solution: AFC: r = assimilation rate / crystallization rate. Trace element + isotope modeling.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquitard is a geological unit that yields little water to wells but may store and transmit water slowly; such a unit is:
options: A coarse grained unit that yields large quantities of water very easily to pumping wells
A unit that only stores water and never transmits it to wells during pumping
Low permeability unit (silt, clay, shale). Poor yield, may store/transmit slowly
A highly permeable formation such as clean gravel or heavily fractured rock of granite
questions.solution: Aquitard: retards vertical flow. Leakage through aquitard → aquitard-aquifer system.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The hexagonal crystal system is defined by which arrangement of crystallographic axes?
options: 4 equal axes in one plane (90°) and a longer perpendicular axis
3 equal axes in plane (120°) and 1 perpendicular axis
3 equal axes at right angles and one inclined axis of different length
3 unequal axes all inclined to one another at oblique angles
questions.solution: Hexagonal: a₁=a₂=a₃≠c, α=β=90°, γ=120°. 6-fold symmetry. Quartz, beryl.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mohr-Coulomb failure criterion: τ = c + σ_n·tan(φ). For c=10MPa, φ=30°, σ_n=50MPa:
options: τ_f = 50×0.577 = 28.9MPa, excluding the cohesion intercept

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mantle convection: evidence from seismic tomography:
options: All same velocity. Tomography shows a perfectly uniform mantle with no anomalies
No evidence. Seismic tomography cannot resolve any structure below the crust
Low-velocity anomalies = hot (upwelling). High-velocity = cold (subducted slab)
Random. Velocity anomalies bear no relationship to temperature or subducted slabs
questions.solution: Seismic tomography: 3D velocity model. Low V = hot mantle. High V = cold subducted slab.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Differential thermal analysis (DTA) of minerals detects which kinds of thermal effects?
options: Endothermic and exothermic reactions in minerals
Only changes in the mass of the sample with heating
Only variation in the density of the heated sample
Only variation in magnetic susceptibility with temperature
questions.solution: DTA: measures temperature difference between sample and reference.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock retains 12.5% of its original parent isotope (half-life 1.3 Gyr). Its radiometric age is about:
options: 3.9 Gyr
5.2 Gyr
0.43 Gyr
1.3 Gyr
questions.solution: 12.5% remaining ⇒ 3 half-lives ⇒ age = 3×1.3 = 3.9 Gyr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater contamination plume migrates:
options: Downgradient from source with dispersion
Upgradient
In all directions equally
Only vertically downward to the water table
questions.solution: Plume: follows hydraulic gradient. Advection (bulk flow) + dispersion (spreading). Density effects if DNAPL/LNAPL.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A P-wave travels at 7 km/s and arrives 30 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 105 km
0.2 km
210 km
30 km
questions.solution: distance = velocity × time = 7×30 = 210 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes the channel pattern, sediment load and discharge of a braided river?
options: River with a single deep channel and no mid-channel bars at all in the river
Multiple channels, bars (mid-channel). High sediment load, variable discharge
Sinuous single channel with point bars and cut banks developed along its course
Perfectly straight channel with a uniform width and gradient throughout the whole course of the river
questions.solution: Braided: bars (longitudinal, transverse, point). Channel bifurcation. High energy.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Massif-type anorthosites are dominantly Proterozoic, plagioclase-rich (>90%) intrusions composed mainly of:
options: Ultramafic bodies composed chiefly of olivine and orthopyroxene cumulates
Proterozoic (1.3-1.0 Ga). Plagioclase-rich (>90%). Andesine-labradorite. Adirondacks, Rogaland
Mafic cumulates rich in clinopyroxene and magnetite formed by gravitational settling of crystals
Granitic intrusions associated with convergent margin magmatism
questions.solution: Anorthosite: Al-rich crustal source? Intrusion at deep crustal levels. Associated with rapakivi granite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Oxygen isotope δ¹⁸O in marine carbonates:
options: No dependence on the water temperature
Isotopic values vary randomly between samples
More positive (enriched) = cooler water, more negative = warmer
More negative (depleted) = warmer climate or freshwater input
questions.solution: δ¹⁸O: foraminifera. More ¹⁶O in warm periods (less ice). δ¹⁸O increase = cooling/ice growth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Evaporite sequence — ideal brine concentration:
options: Calcite → Gypsum → Halite → K-Mg salts (sylvite, carnallite). 20× seawater concentration for halite
Halite → Gypsum → Calcite → K-Mg salts, with calcite precipitating only at the highest brine concentrations
K-Mg salts → Halite → Gypsum → Calcite, with gypsum precipitating last at saturation
K-Mg salts precipitate first at low concentration, followed by halite and finally calcite
questions.solution: Evaporite: restricted basin. Dead Sea, Great Salt Lake. Salt giants: Messinian (5.96-5.33 Ma).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the visible and near-infrared regions, how does the reflectance of clear water typically change with wavelength?
options: High reflectance in blue, decreasing toward NIR
High reflectance in all wavelength bands equally
Highest reflectance in the near-infrared region
Very low reflectance in all wavelength bands
questions.solution: Water absorbs NIR strongly. Reflects blue-green.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 25% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Continental collision: India-Asia collision (~55 Ma):
options: The Indian plate continued subducting beneath Asia without any continental contact
Himalayan orogeny began 200 Ma ago with the closure of the entire Paleo-Tethys ocean
Tethys ocean closed. Himalayan orogeny. Tibetan Plateau uplift
The Tibetan Plateau subsided below sea level forming a foreland basin sequence
questions.solution: India: northward drift ~20 cm/yr. Collision ~55 Ma. Himalaya: MCT, MBT, MFT. Tibet: thickened crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In mineral flotation, selective separation of minerals is achieved by attachment of particles to what?
options: Magnetic separation of particles by exploiting differences in their magnetic susceptibility and coercivity
Selective attachment of mineral particles to air bubbles. Collectors, frothers, modifiers
Gravity separation using jigs, spirals and shaking tables on dense slurries
Chemical precipitation of dissolved metals by controlled addition of reagents
questions.solution: Flotation: surface chemistry. Collector (xanthate for sulfides). Frother (pine oil). pH modifier.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does permeability measure, and what does it depend on in a sedimentary rock?
options: Ability to transmit fluids. Depends on pore connectivity, not just porosity
Ability of a rock to store fluids, controlled entirely by total pore volume
Identical to porosity in every respect, with no independent controlling factors
Always exactly twice the porosity regardless of grain size or cement content
questions.solution: Perm: k = Q·μ·L/(A·ΔP) (Darcy's law). Shale: high porosity, very low perm.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do the Raniganj, Barakar, and Karharbari formations compare in coal quality and rank?
options: Karharbari is the best rank with the highest coking quality among all seams
No ranking exists since all Indian Gondwana coals are identical in rank
Equal quality and rank of coal across all the Gondwana coal-bearing formations
Raniganj > Barakar > Karharbari (quality and rank)
questions.solution: Raniganj: high rank, good coking. Barakar: good quality. Karharbari: early, lower rank.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pegmatite rare-element deposits: LCT type enriched in:
options: Lead, tin and tungsten as scheelite and cassiterite
Li, Cs, Ta, Nb, Be, Rb
Copper, nickel and zinc concentrated by magmatic segregation
Iron, manganese and chromium in oxide and silicate phases
questions.solution: LCT: Li-Cs-Ta pegmatites. NYF: Nb-Y-F. Economic: spodumene (Li), columbite-tantalite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a concordant tabular igneous intrusion that lies parallel to bedding?
options: Discordant intrusion that cuts across the bedding at a steep angle
Concordant tabular intrusion (parallel to bedding)
Vertical sheet-like intrusion emplaced along fractures and joint planes
Discordant body injected across the regional structure of the area
questions.solution: Sill: horizontal sheet. Examples: Palisades Sill, Whin Sill.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Phase diagram: ternary (plagioclase-quartz-K-feldspar) for granitic rocks. Thermal valley:
options: Minimum melt composition near granite (600-700°C at 200MPa H₂O)
Melt composition identical to the most refractory basalt in the system
Dioritic composition marking the highest temperature melting point
Composition at which no melting can ever occur in this ternary system
questions.solution: Ternary minimum: granitic minimum melt. Low melting point of felsic system. Explains granite abundance.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Basalt: most common volcanic rock. Ocean floor composition:
options: Tholeiitic basalt (low K, low TiO2)
Alkaline basalt enriched in potassium, titanium and incompatible elements
Andesite typical of continental margin volcanic arcs
Rhyolite produced by advanced fractional crystallisation
questions.solution: MORB: tholeiitic. Depleted mantle source. Low K2O, TiO2. Pillow lavas on ocean floor.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Trace element discrimination diagram for tectonic setting: TiO₂ vs Zr for basalts. MORB:
options: Low TiO₂, Zr (15-90 ppm)
High titania with zirconium exceeding several hundred parts per million
Basalt completely devoid of zirconium in its trace element budget
High zirconium with titania well above the mid-ocean ridge average
questions.solution: MORB: depleted. OIB: enriched (high Ti, Zr). Island arc: low Ti, variable Zr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the relative duration of the Precambrian, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic in the geological time scale?
options: All eras are of equal duration across the entire geological time scale of the Earth history
Precambrian is the shortest interval, covering less than 10% of Earth's recorded geological history
Precambrian (88%), Paleozoic (545-251 Ma), Mesozoic (251-66 Ma), Cenozoic (66 Ma-present)
Cenozoic is the longest era, spanning nearly half of the total Earth history span recorded
questions.solution: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (Precambrian). Phanerozoic: Paleo-Meso-Cenozoic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the Folk classification, how are limestone allochems combined with matrix or cement to classify the rock?
options: Classification based solely on the grain-size distribution of the sediment, ignoring grain type and cement
Classification based solely on colour and organic matter content of the carbonate
Allochens (grains) + orthocherms (matrix/cement). Skeletal, ooids, peloids, intraclasts
Classification based solely on the bedding and lamination thickness of the limestone
questions.solution: Folk: Sparry calcite cement = sparry allochemical. Micrite = microcrystalline ooze.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pseudotachylite, a glassy rock found along faults, forms by which process during earthquakes?
options: Cataclasite formed by slow brittle crushing without any melting
Mylonite formed by ductile flow at high temperature and pressure
Friction melt along fault. Glassy/aphantic. Co-seismic melting
Hornfels produced by heat from a nearby igneous intrusion
questions.solution: Pseudotachylite: rapid frictional heating. Pseudotachylite veins. Vredefort impact structure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) produces a 2D or 3D subsurface image by measuring:
options: 2D/3D resistivity imaging. Dipole-dipole, Wenner, Schlumberger arrays. For contamination, cavity, archaeology
One dimensional vertical electrical sounding with the current electrodes expanded about a single fixed centre point of the spread
Mapping of magnetic susceptibility contrasts for locating buried ferrous metallic objects
Measurement of natural electric and magnetic fields at the surface to image deep crustal resistivity
questions.solution: ERT: multi-electrode. Pseudo-section. Inversion. Time-lapse ERT for process monitoring.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In porphyry copper systems, alteration zones from the center outward follow which sequence?
options: Sodic-calcic alteration confined to the surrounding metamorphic aureole, absent inside the intrusion
Potassic (center) → phyllic → argillic → propylitic (outer). Sericite, chlorite, clay
A single quartz-sericite zone enveloping the entire stockwork vein system
Irregular distribution controlled solely by the fracture density of the host rock
questions.solution: Porphyry: Cu-Mo. Low grade (0.3-1% Cu). Large tonnage. Stockwork veins. Chile, USA, Indonesia.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Radiometric dating works because a radioactive parent isotope decays to a daughter at a rate set by its:
options: Depth of burial below the Earth's surface
Constant half-life
Pressure prevailing at the site of formation
Temperature of the surrounding environment
questions.solution: Decay is exponential with a fixed half-life, so the parent/daughter ratio gives an absolute age.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 50 m on flat ground and dips at 35°. Its true thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 50×sin35° ≈ 28.68 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 2 m thick, with density 1.4 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 2.0 Mt
2.8 Mt
1.4 Mt
5.6 Mt
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×2 m×1.4 t/m³ ≈ 2.8 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer is best defined as a saturated, permeable geological unit that:
options: A dry rock unit that stores no water at all within it
Saturated permeable unit that yields useful water quantity
A low permeability unit that retards the flow of groundwater
An impermeable unit that blocks the vertical movement of water
questions.solution: Aquifer: sand/gravel, sandstone, fractured limestone, basalt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What approximate specific gravity value does the mineral barite possess?
options: ~4.5 (heavy for non-metallic)
~2.5 typical of common rock-forming silicates
~6.5 higher than most metallic ore minerals
~3.5 comparable to the average mineral value
questions.solution: Barite (BaSO4) — high SG. Used as drilling mud additive.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Cliffs, wave-cut platforms, sea stacks, sea arches, beaches, bars and lagoons are landforms characteristic of which environment?
options: Coastal landforms are limited only to volcanic shorelines of the world
Coastal landforms are limited only to deltaic plains and estuaries
Cliffs, wave-cut platform, sea stack, sea arch, beach, bar, lagoon
Coastal landforms are limited only to glacial fjord coasts of the world
questions.solution: Coastal: erosion (cliffs, stacks) and deposition (beaches, bars, spits).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which preprocessing step removes geometric distortions using ground control points and produces a map-projected, orthorectified image?
options: Resampling the image, using only the scene corner coordinates that are provided within the metadata file
Assigning the map coordinates only approximately, and accepting the large residual errors that result from it
Applying a standard map projection to the image, without correcting for the sensor-induced distortion
Remove geometric distortions. Map projection. GCPs. RMSE < 1 pixel. Orthorectification
questions.solution: Geometric: model sensor + terrain. GCP: ground control points. Resampling: nearest, bilinear, cubic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Geosynthetics in slope stabilization: geogrids provide:
options: Tensile reinforcement and soil confinement
Purely as a drainage layer for removing groundwater
As a waterproof membrane to stop all infiltration
As a chemical stabilizer that changes the soil mineralogy
questions.solution: Geogrids: high tensile strength, interlock with soil. Geotextiles: filtration, separation. Geomembranes: waterproofing.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which volcanic texture shows aligned feldspar microlites produced by flow alignment?
options: Porphyritic fabric with large crystals in a fine-grained groundmass
Glassy texture formed by rapid cooling without crystal alignment
Random orientation of equant crystals typical of massive lavas
Aligned feldspar microlites in volcanic rock. Flow alignment
questions.solution: Trachytic: parallel alignment of plagioclase. Indicates flow direction in lava.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The law of superposition states that, in an undisturbed sequence, the oldest layer is:
options: In the middle
At the bottom
At the top
Randomly placed
questions.solution: Sediments are deposited oldest-first, so the lowest undisturbed bed is the oldest.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How does the storm-dominated shelf facies model divide the shoreface using the fair-weather wave base?
options: Fair-weather wave base divides upper shoreface (high energy) from lower shoreface (low energy)
A single uniform energy level operates throughout the shelf at all depths and times
No wave base exists, and energy increases continuously with depth in all settings
Energy decreases monotonically with depth, with no distinct fair-weather or storm wave base surfaces recognized at all
questions.solution: Upper: cross-bedded sand. Lower: hummocky cross-stratification (HCS). Storm deposits.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mylonite, a foliated rock from ductile shear zones, forms chiefly by which process?
options: Coarse-grained rock formed by static recrystallization under heat alone without deformation
Brecciated rock containing angular clasts produced by brittle faulting without any subsequent recrystallization or melting
Impact melt glass formed by frictional heating during a large meteorite impact event
Fine-grained, foliated rock in ductile shear zone. Grain size reduction by dynamic recrystallization
questions.solution: Mylonite: ductile deformation. Porphyroclasts in fine matrix. S-C fabrics. Protomylonite→mylonite→ultramylonite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: At a station the S-wave arrives 5 s after the P-wave. Using ~8 km per second of S–P delay, the epicentral distance is about:
options: 5 km
20 km
80 km
40 km
questions.solution: distance ≈ (S−P time) × 8 km/s = 5×8 = 40 km.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An ore body of 1 Mt has an average metal grade of 1%. The contained metal is about:
options: 1 kt
5 kt
20 kt
10 kt
questions.solution: Metal = tonnage × grade = 1 Mt × 1% = 10 thousand tonnes (kt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: (U-Th)/He dating measures ⁴He produced by alpha decay and, with its low temperature sensitivity, is used to reconstruct:
options: Fission track method applied to apatite grains of the rock that is being examined in detail
Rb-Sr method applied to whole-rock samples of the same rock suite and its constituent bodies
⁴He from α decay. Low T sensitivity (apatite ~70°C). Provided for exhumation/burial history
K-Ar method applied to potassium minerals of the ash layers in the sedimentary sequence
questions.solution: (U-Th)/He: thermochronology. He diffusion rate. Apatite (AHe), zircon (ZHe).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 20 m over a horizontal distance of 20 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(20/20) ≈ 45°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The section shows 20 m of overburden above a 5 m coal seam. The volumetric stripping ratio (overburden : coal thickness) is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 20/5 = 4 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A rock sample of 100 cm³ contains 20 cm³ of pore space. Its porosity is:
questions.solution: Porosity = (void volume/total volume)×100 = 20/100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What causes the undulose extinction observed in strained quartz grains under crossed polars?
options: Parallel extinction when cleavages lie along the polarizer
Symmetric extinction about both cleavage directions
Straight extinction shown by every quartz grain
Gradual extinction (wavey) due to strain
questions.solution: Undulose extinction: common in deformed quartz. Indicates stress history.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes a hyperspectral sensor from a multispectral sensor in terms of the number and width of its bands?
options: Hyperspectral has many narrow contiguous bands
Multispectral has many narrow contiguous bands
Both systems have the same number of bands
Hyperspectral has fewer, wider spectral bands
questions.solution: Multispectral: 3-10 broad bands. Hyperspectral: 100+ narrow.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which texture, with elongated olivine blades, is characteristic of komatiites?
options: Spinifex texture (elongated olivine blades)
Interlocking granular texture formed by equal-size equant crystals of plagioclase
Porphyritic texture with large quartz and feldspar phenocrysts in a glassy base
Ophitic texture defined by plagioclase laths enclosed in pyroxene oikocrysts
questions.solution: Komatiite: Archean ultramafic volcanic. Spinifex due to rapid cooling.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What does graded bedding, with coarsest material at the bottom, indicate about the depositional process?
options: Coarsest at bottom, fining upward (turbidity current)
Reverse grading with the coarsest material at the top of each bed
Coarsest material at the top and finest material at the bottom of the bed
Uniform grain size throughout the bed, with no vertical size trend at all
questions.solution: Graded: Bouma sequence in turbidites. Normal (fining up) or inverse (coarsening up).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Seismic reflection: CMP (common midpoint) stacking improves:
options: Vertical resolution by broadening the seismic frequency bandwidth
Only the lateral resolution of the migrated section at fold
Frequency content of the data at the expense of deeper penetration
Signal-to-noise ratio by factor of √n (n=stacking fold)
questions.solution: CMP: multiple traces with same midpoint. Stack: improves S/N. NMO correction before stacking.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 1 km², is 5 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 5 Mt
3.3 Mt
13 Mt
6.5 Mt
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 1×10⁶ m²×5 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 6.5 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes a knickpoint, its appearance in a river profile and its main causes?
options: Sediment body deposited where a river enters a lake or sea and spreads out over the bed of the basin floor below
Sinuous bend in a river with a cut bank and a point bar developed along its course
Break in river profile (waterfall). Caused by base level fall, resistant rock, fault
Flat area of the valley floor that is inundated during periods of flood of the river water
questions.solution: Knickpoint: migrates upstream as river adjusts to new base level. Rejuvenation head.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Carbonatite: igneous rock with >50% carbonate minerals. Key economic minerals:
options: REE (monazite, bastnäschite), Nb (pyrochlore), P (apatite)
Copper and zinc sulfides associated with porphyry and skarn deposits
Gold and silver in quartz veins and stockwork fracture systems
Iron ore in banded oxide and carbonate facies of the deposit
questions.solution: Carbonatite: Oldoinyo Lengai (Tanzania). Only active carbonatite volcano. REE deposits.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which type of unconformity exists where sedimentary rocks overlie igneous or metamorphic basement rocks?
options: Sedimentary rocks overlie tilted older sedimentary rocks at a high angle
Sedimentary rocks overlie a lava flow with the same dip and strike direction
Igneous rocks overlie sedimentary rocks that have never been eroded or tilted
Sedimentary rocks overlie igneous/metamorphic basement
questions.solution: Nonconformity: erosion of basement + deposition. Basal conglomerate common.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sequence of DEM operations, from sink filling to pour point, is followed in GIS to delineate a watershed?
options: DEM → fill → flow direction → flow accumulation → pour point → watershed. Arc Hydro, TauDEM
Watershed boundaries are delineated by hand on paper maps without using any digital elevation model at all
Only visual interpretation of contour lines on the topographic map
A purely manual delineation carried out on paper maps
questions.solution: Watershed: area draining to outlet. Sub-basins: stream ordering (Strahler, Shreve). Topographic wetness index.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A fracture in rock along which there has been observable displacement is a:
options: Joint
Cleavage
Bedding plane
Fault
questions.solution: Faults show relative movement of the two blocks; joints show none.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which type of data, giving high-resolution three-dimensional detail of terrain and vegetation canopy, is provided by LiDAR?
options: High-resolution 3D terrain and canopy data
Only cloud top temperature measurements from orbit
Only sea surface temperature readings from orbit
Only coarse 1 km resolution elevation grids
questions.solution: LiDAR: laser pulses measure distance. Creates DEMs.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Pumping test analysis: Theis equation s = Q·W(u)/(4πT). W(u) is:
options: Power function of the dimensionless time parameter u
Logarithmic function valid for all values of the parameter
Well function (exponential integral)
Linear function of the drawdown at the pumping well
questions.solution: W(u) = -0.5772-ln(u)+u-u²/... (series). u = r²S/(4Tt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of artificial groundwater recharge?
options: Only riverbank filtration of surface water along the banks of the perennial rivers of the region
Check dams, recharge wells, percolation tanks, roof-top harvesting, injection wells
Only the pumping of groundwater from deep production wells during a prolonged drought period of the year
Only seawater intrusion barriers that are built along the coastal belt of the open sea
questions.solution: MAR: aquifer storage and recovery (ASR). Water quality treatment. Clogging management.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What type of cleavage do the minerals of the mica group characteristically show?
options: Perfect cubic cleavage in three directions
Three cleavage directions at approximately 75°
Two cleavage directions meeting at about 90°
One perfect basal cleavage
questions.solution: Mica splits into thin sheets. Muscovite (white) and biotite (black).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 10% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 15% ash. Its fixed carbon is:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal sample (proximate analysis) has 5% moisture, 35% volatile matter and 10% ash. Its fixed carbon is:
questions.solution: Fixed C = 100 − (moisture + VM + ash) = 100 − (5+35+10) = 50%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 20 m over a horizontal distance of 40 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(20/40) ≈ 26.6°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the approximate specific gravity value of the common mineral quartz?
questions.solution: Quartz SG ~2.65. Heavy minerals have SG > 2.85.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Groundwater in alluvial aquifers is characterized by high porosity and storage, sustainable yields, and recharge from:
options: Porous, high storage. Sustainable yields. River recharge
Fracture-dependent with storage limited to the joints and cracks
Low storage capacity with yields controlled by secondary porosity
Low yield everywhere and no connection with the river system
questions.solution: Alluvium: sand/gravel aquifers. Good quality. Near-river zones have high recharge.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 2 km², is 2 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
options: 2.6 Mt
5.2 Mt
4 Mt
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 2×10⁶ m²×2 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 5.2 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed dipping at 60° shows a width of 40 m across a horizontal surface. Its true (perpendicular) thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = width × sin(dip) = 40×sin60° ≈ 34.64 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Rslickenline (striae on fault surface) indicates:
options: The stress orientation present at the time the fault was formed
The age of the fault relative to the surrounding rock units
Direction of last movement on fault
The lithology in which the fault surface has developed
questions.solution: Slickenlines: linear features on fault surface. Mineral fibers grow in slip direction.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is an intrusive igneous body smaller than a batholith (<100 km²)?
options: Igneous body that is exactly the same size as a batholith in outcrop area
Intrusion larger than a batholith extending over hundreds of square km
Volcanic landform built of lava flows and pyroclastic material around a vent
Smaller than batholith (<100 km²)
questions.solution: Stock: similar to batholith but smaller. Often associated with mineral deposits.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Shear sense indicators — sigma (σ) porphyroclast:
options: Mica fish with asymmetric tails that record the shear sense
Tails at angle to foliation. σ_a (asymmetric tails on both sides) and σ_c (tails in pressure shadow)
Delta porphyroclast with curved recrystallized tails that spiral completely around the rigid central grain
S-C fabric with oblique schistosity and discrete shear bands
questions.solution: σ: tails parallel to shear direction. σ-type: tails merge in matrix. δ-type: tails embayed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following lists the main components of the hydrologic cycle?
options: Only condensation, evaporation and cloud formation within the atmosphere
Only percolation and the movement of soil moisture through the entire unsaturated zone
Precipitation, evapotranspiration, runoff, infiltration, percolation, groundwater flow
Only infiltration of rainfall and its subsequent return as surface runoff flow
questions.solution: Water balance: P = R + ET + ΔS. Global: 70% evapotranspiration, 30% runoff.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Packer tests in boreholes are used to isolate and measure the permeability of:
options: Specific depth intervals in borehole for permeability measurement
The entire borehole so that the full saturated aquifer thickness is tested
Surface water bodies from the influence of the borehole test
Only the aquitard layers that bound the main aquifer under test
questions.solution: Packer test: inflatable packers seal interval. Pump or slug test in isolated zone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is computed using which two spectral bands of a sensor?
options: Red and Near-Infrared bands
Blue and green visible bands
Thermal and microwave bands
SWIR and TIR wavelength bands
questions.solution: NDVI = (NIR - Red)/(NIR + Red). High = healthy vegetation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A mineral that effervesces (fizzes) when dilute hydrochloric acid is applied is:
options: Feldspar
Quartz
Calcite
Garnet
questions.solution: Calcite (CaCO₃) reacts with dilute HCl, releasing CO₂ — a standard field test.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What characteristics should a good index (guide) fossil possess?
options: Widespread but short-lived in geologic time
Rare and confined to a single basin with an extremely long stratigraphic range
Found in igneous and metamorphic rocks, permitting absolute-age dating of plutons
Geographically restricted to one locality but present in almost every rock formation there
questions.solution: Wide distribution plus a short time range makes a fossil useful for correlation/dating.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Evaporation is measured with a Class A evaporation pan and converted to lake evaporation using:
options: Class A evaporation pan. Pan coefficient (0.7-0.8) to convert to lake evaporation
Direct measurement of the total volume of water lost from the surface of the lake by evaporation
Pan evaporation readings that require no conversion factor of any kind to be applied
Measurement of the evaporation losses using a standard recording rain gauge instrument
questions.solution: Class A pan: 1.2m diameter, 0.25m deep. Pan evaporation > lake evaporation (K_p).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which spaceborne sensor carries the MSI instrument with 13 bands, a 5-day revisit, and is suited to vegetation and agriculture?
options: The OLI sensor, with 9 spectral bands at 30m resolution and a 16-day revisit period
The MODIS sensor, with 36 spectral bands at 250-1000m for daily global coverage
The ETM+ sensor, with 8 bands, a 15m panchromatic band, and a 16-day revisit period
MSI (13 bands, 10-60m). 5-day revisit. 290km swath. Vegetation, agriculture

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What type of twinning is characteristic of the mineral plagioclase feldspar?
options: Polysynthetic (albite law) — repeated lamellae
Carlsbad simple twinning observed in potassium feldspars only
Cross twins characteristic of staurolite and aragonite
Simple twins formed during rapid magmatic crystallization
questions.solution: Polysynthetic twinning diagnostic of plagioclase under microscope.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a reverse or thrust fault, which way does the hanging wall move, and what dip separates a thrust fault from a reverse fault?
options: Hanging wall moves up (compression). Thrust: <45° dip
Hanging wall moves down relative to the footwall under regional extensional stress
Both blocks move horizontally past each other with no vertical component at all
Footwall is displaced upward relative to the hanging wall under pure extension
questions.solution: Reverse: shortening. Thrust: low angle (<45°). Nappes: large displacement thrusts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: To extract 15 m³ of coal, 45 m³ of overburden must be removed. The stripping ratio is:
questions.solution: Stripping ratio = overburden/coal = 45/15 = 3 : 1.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Thermal infrared remote sensing measures:
options: Surface temperature and emissivity
Vegetation health through chlorophyll content
Soil moisture in the root zone directly
Water depth through penetration of the column
questions.solution: TIR: 8-14 um wavelength. Detects emitted thermal radiation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes solifluction and the alternative name by which the process is known?
options: Rapid free fall of rock fragments from a steep cliff face to the base of the slope
Fast-moving flow of water-saturated material down a steep slope in a short time
Downslope movement of dry granular material under the influence of gravity with no water involved
Slow downslope flow of water-saturated soil over permafrost. Gelifluction
questions.solution: Solifluction: lobes, sheets. 1-10 cm/yr. Gelifluction: thaw of ice lenses. Terrace-like landforms.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is a pyroclastic flow deposit whose glass shards fuse at high temperature?
options: Lava flow that cools to form a dense aphanitic rock with prominent flow banding
Air-fall tephra layer that accumulates without any subsequent welding
Sedimentary deposit of reworked ash and pumice laid down in water
Pyroclastic flow deposit. Welded: glass shards fused at high temperature
questions.solution: Ignimbrite: welded pyroclastic. High temperature (>600°C) → welding. Devitrification of glass shards.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Crystal system with 6-fold symmetry axis is:
options: Hexagonal
Cubic
Tetragonal
Orthorhombic
questions.solution: Hexagonal: one 6-fold axis.
